verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              भीमसेनं च पाञ्चाल्यं चेदिकेकयसंवृतम् । वैकर्तनः स्वयं रुद्ध्वा वारयामास सायकैः ॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said After this Vaikartana, himself resisting Bhimasena aided by the king of Panchala, Chedi and Kaikeya, showered numberless arrows upon him.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तु चेदिकारूषान्सृञ्जयांश्च महारथान् । कर्णो जघान समरे भीमसेनस्य पश्यतः ॥२॥
verses.english: Karna killed in the battle many strong carwarriors of the Chedis, Karushas and Srinjayas in the very presence of Bhimasena.

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनस्ततः कर्णं विहाय रथसत्तमम् । प्रययौ कौरवं सैन्यं कक्षमग्निरिव ज्वलन् ॥३॥
verses.english: Then Bhimasena leaving Karna, the most powerful car-warrior, rushed towards the Kaurava force like a blazing forest fire.

verses.sanskrit: सूतपुत्रोऽपि समरे पञ्चालान्केकयांस्तथा । सृञ्जयांश्च महेष्वासान्निजघान सहस्रशः ॥४॥
verses.english: The Suta's son too began to slay by thousands the mighty bowmen of the Panchalas, the Kaikeyas and the Srinjayas.

verses.sanskrit: संशप्तकेषु पार्थश्च कौरवेषु वृकोदरः । पञ्चालेषु तथा कर्णः क्षयं चक्रुर्महारथाः ॥५॥
verses.english: Indeed, the mighty car-warriors Karna, Partha and Vrikodera began to annihilate the Panchalas, Samasaptakas and Kauravas respectively.

verses.sanskrit: ते क्षत्रिया दह्यमानास्त्रिभिस्तैः पावकोपमैः । जग्मुर्विनाशं समरे राजन् दुर्मन्त्रिते तव ॥६॥
verses.english: For your bad policy, O king, all these Kshatriyas, burnt down, as it were, by those three heroes resembling three burning flames, got exterminated.

verses.sanskrit: ततो दुर्योधनः क्रुद्धो नकुलं नवभिः शरैः । विव्याध भरतश्रेष्ठ चतुरश्चास्य वाजिनः ॥७॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O foremost of the Bharatas, Duryodhana, being enraged, pierced Nakula and the four holes of his car with nine arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ततः पुनरमेयात्मा तव पुत्रो जनाधिप । क्षुरेण सहदेवस्य ध्वजं चिच्छेद काञ्चनम् ॥८॥
verses.english: Then again, O lord of men, your highly energetic son cut down the golden standard of Shahadeva with a razor.

verses.sanskrit: नकुलस्तु ततः क्रुद्धस्तव पुत्रं च सप्तभिः । जघान समरे राजन् सहदेवश्च पञ्चभिः ॥९॥
verses.english: Nakula then, O king, being greatly enraged, struck you son with seventy three arrows and Sahadeva with five. Filled with anger he struck.

verses.sanskrit: तावुभौ भरतश्रेष्ठौ ज्येष्ठौ सर्वधनुष्मताम् । विव्याधोरसि संक्रुद्धः पञ्चभिः पञ्चभिः शरैः ॥१०॥
verses.english: Then both of those great warriors of the Bharata race and the foremost of bowmen, on the breast with five arrows each.

verses.sanskrit: ततो पराभ्यां भल्लाभ्यां धनुषी समकृन्तत । यमयोः सहसा राजन्विव्याध च त्रिसप्तभिः ॥११॥
verses.english: Then he cut-off the bows of both of those two warriors with two of his broad-pointed arrows and suddenly, O king he pierced both of them with twenty-one arrows.

verses.sanskrit: तावन्ये धनुषी श्रेष्ठे शक्रचापनिभे शुभे । प्रगृह्य रेजतुः शूरौ देवपुत्रसमौ युधि ॥१२॥
verses.english: Each of them, taking up two beautiful bows resembling those of Indra's looked very graceful like two celestial youths in the battlefield.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तौ रभसौ युद्धे भ्रातरौ भ्रातरं युधि । शरैर्ववृषतुर्घोरैर्महामेघौ यथाऽचलम् ॥१३॥
verses.english: Then, O king, those two brothers, greatly active in battle, began to throw terrible shafts in ceaseless torrents upon their cousins like two great masses of thick clouds pouring their contents on the hills.

verses.sanskrit: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज तव पुत्रो महारथः । पाण्डुपुत्रौ महेष्वासौ वारयामास पत्रिभिः ॥१४॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O king, your son, the great carwarrior, being greatly enraged resisted those the rays twin sons of Pandu, the great bowmen, with numberless arrows.

verses.sanskrit: धनुर्मण्डलमेवास्य दृश्यते युधि भारत । सायकाश्चैव दृश्यन्ते निश्चरन्तः समन्ततः ॥१५॥
verses.english: The bow of your son, O Bharata, was repeatedly drawn to a circle and the arrows were ceaselessly issued from it towards all directions covered with Duryodhana's arrows those sons of Pandu ceased to shine brightly as the sun and the moon lose their splendour when enveloped with a mass of dark clouds. Indeed, O king, those gold-winged arrows, sharpened on stone, covered all the sides like of the sun.

verses.sanskrit: आच्छादयन्दिशः सर्वाः सूर्यस्येवांशवो यथा । बाणभूते ततस्तस्मिन्संछन्ने च नभस्तले ॥१६॥
verses.english: When the firinament was thus covered and the whole sky looked like a sheet of arrows the twin brothers appeared like the destroyer himself.

verses.sanskrit: यमाभ्यां ददृशे रूपं कालान्तकयमोपमम् । पराक्रमं तु तं दृष्ट्वा तव सूनोर्महारथाः ॥१७॥
verses.english: But, on the other hand, beholding the valour of your son all the car-warriors took the twin sons of Madri to be at the point of death.

verses.sanskrit: मृत्योरुपान्तिकं प्राप्तौ माद्रीपुत्रौ स्म मेनिरे । ततः सेनापती राजन्पाण्डवस्य महारथः ॥१८॥
पार्षतः प्रययौ तत्र यत्र राजा सुयोधनः । माद्रीपुत्रौ ततः शूरौ व्यतिक्रम्य महारथौ ॥१९॥
verses.english: Then, O king, the mighty car-warrior Parsata, the commander of the Pandava army, went towards the direction of Suyodhana (Duryodhana).

verses.sanskrit: धृष्टद्युम्नस्तव सुतं वारयामास सायकैः । तमविध्यदमेयात्मा तव पुत्रो ह्यमर्षणः ॥२०॥
verses.english: Violating the regimental order of those two great car-warriors, the two brave sons of Madri, Dhristadyumna began to oppose your son with his arrows.

verses.sanskrit: पाञ्चाल्यं पञ्चविंशत्या प्रहसन् पुरुषर्षभः । ततः पुनरमेयात्मा तव पुत्रो ह्यमर्षणः ॥२१॥
verses.english: Then that highly energetic hero, your son, the foremost of men, full of revengeful spirit and smiling scoffingły, struck the prince of the Panchalas with twenty-five arrows.

verses.sanskrit: विद्ध्वा ननाद पाञ्चाल्यं षष्ट्या पञ्चभिरेव च । तथाऽस्य सशरं चापं हस्तावापं च मारिष ॥२२॥
verses.english: Again the most energetic son of yours, actuated by the eager desire of taking revenge, struck the Panchala prince once with sixty arrows and again with five and roared aloud.

verses.sanskrit: क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन राजा चिच्छेद संयुगे । तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं पाञ्चाल्यः शत्रुकर्शनः ॥२३॥
verses.english: Then the king, O sire, cut-off, in the fight, with his razor-shaped arrow his enemy's bow and the leathern fence with the arrows fixed thereon.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यदादत्त वेगेन धनुर्भारसहं नवम् । प्रज्वलन्निव वेगेन संरंभाद्रुधिरेक्षणः ॥२४॥
verses.english: Throwing away that broken bow, that oppressor of foes, the prince of Panchala, quickly took up a new and more elastic one.

verses.sanskrit: अशोभत महेष्वासो धृष्टद्युम्नः कृतव्रणः । स पञ्चदश नाराचान् श्वसतः पन्नगानिव ॥२५॥
verses.english: Then that great bowman, Dhristadyumna, with blood-shot eyes, shone on his car like a burning flame.

verses.sanskrit: जिघांसुर्भरतश्रेष्ठं धृष्टद्युम्नो व्यपासृजत् । ते वर्म हेमविकृतं भित्त्वा राज्ञः शिलाशिताः ॥२६॥
verses.english: Then, O chief of Bharatas, the hero Dhristadyumna, bent bent upon killing him, discharged fifteen sharp shafts, called Narachas, which looked like hissing serpents.

verses.sanskrit: विविशुर्वसुधां वेगात्कङ्कबर्हिणवाससः । सोऽतिविद्धो महाराज पुत्रस्तेऽतिव्यराजत ॥२७॥
वसन्तकाले सुमहान् प्रफुल्ल इव किंशुकः । स छिन्नवर्मा नाराचप्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतः ॥२८॥
verses.english: Being deeply wounded, O king, your son looked exceedingly grand like a Kinshuka tree full of flowers in the spring.

verses.sanskrit: धृष्टद्युम्नस्य भल्लेन क्रुद्धश्चिच्छेद कार्मुकम् । अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं त्वरमाणो महीपतिः ॥२९॥
verses.english: His armour being thus cut through and himself being fatigued with the wounds and his feelings being awfully excited he cut-off Dhristadyumna's bow with a broad pointed arrow.

verses.sanskrit: सायकैर्दशभी राजन् भ्रुवोर्मध्ये समार्पयत् । तस्य तेऽशोभयन्वक्त्रं कर्मारपरिमार्जिताः ॥३०॥
verses.english: Then, O lord of the earth, the king penetrated ten arrows into the forehead of his assailant whose bow had already been cut-off by him.

verses.sanskrit: प्रफुल्लं पङ्कजं यद्वद्भ्रमरा मधुलिप्सवः । त‌दपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं धृष्टद्युम्नो महामनाः ॥३१॥
verses.english: These shafts, polished by the black-smith, looked on the face of Dhristadyumna like so many black bees on a full blown lily desirous of sucking the sweet honey.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यदादत्त वेगेन धनुर्भल्लांश्च षोडश । ततो दुर्योधनस्याश्वान् हत्वा सूतं च पञ्चभिः ॥३२॥
verses.english: Throwing that broken bow aside Dhristadyumna quickly took up another bow and with it sixteen broad-pointed arrows.

verses.sanskrit: धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन जातरूपपरिष्कृतम् । रथं सोपस्करं छत्रं शक्तिं खड्गं गदां ध्वजम् ॥३३॥
verses.english: Then with five of these arrows he slew Duryodhana's four horses and his Suta charioteer and with another he cut-off his gilded bow.

verses.sanskrit: भल्लैश्चिच्छेद दशभिः पुत्रस्य तव पार्षतः । तपनीयाङ्गदं चित्रं नागं मणिमयं शुभम् ॥३४॥
verses.english: And with remaining ten shafts the son of Prishata cut-off the royal umbrella, the spear, the sword, the mace, the car with Upaskara and the flag of your son.

verses.sanskrit: ध्वजं कुरुपतेश्छिन्नं ददृशुः सर्वपार्थिवाः । दुर्योधनं तु विरथं छिन्नवर्मायुधं रणे ॥३५॥
verses.english: Alas, all the chiefs saw the beautiful standard of the Kuru king, adorned with golden Angada and bearing the likeness of an elephant set with jewels, cut-off by Dhristadyumna.

verses.sanskrit: भ्रातरः पर्यरक्षन्त सोदरा भरतर्षभ । तमारोप्य रथे राजन्दण्डधारो जनाधिपः ॥३६॥
verses.english: Then, O foremost of the Bharata's race, Duryodhana, thus deprived of all his weapons in the battle, was protected by his brothers.

verses.sanskrit: अपाहरदसंभ्रान्तो धृष्टद्युम्नस्य पश्यतः । कर्णस्तु सात्यकिं जित्वा राजगृद्धी महाबलः ॥३७॥
verses.english: In the very sight of Dhristadyumna. Dandadhara, taking the king upon his own car, quickly carried him away from the field.

verses.sanskrit: द्रोणहन्तारमुग्रेषुं ससाराभिमुखो रणे । तं पृष्ठतोऽभ्ययात्तूर्णं शैनेयो वितुदञ्छरैः ॥३८॥
verses.english: In the meantime, the greatly powerful Karna, having killed Satyaki, proceeded straight on towards the slayer of Drona for the rescue of the Kuru king.

verses.sanskrit: वारणं जघनोपान्ते विषाणाभ्यामिव द्विपः । स भारत महानासीद्योधानां सुमहात्मनाम् ॥३९॥
verses.english: And the son of Sini speedily pursued him striking him with arrows as an elephant pursues his rival piercing him with his tusks on the rear.

verses.sanskrit: कर्णपार्षतयोर्मध्ये त्वदीयानां महारणः । न पाण्डवानां नास्माकं योधः कश्चित्पराङ्मुखः ॥४०॥
verses.english: Thus, O king, the battle raged furiously amongst these sturdy heroes of both the armies and the spot, lying between Karna and the son of Prishata, grew simply terrifying.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्यदृश्यत्ततः कर्णः पञ्चालांस्त्वरितो ययौ । तस्मिन् क्षणे नरश्रेष्ठ गज-वाजि-जनक्षयः ॥४१॥
verses.english: Not a single combatant, of either party, turned his face from the field. Karna then rushed towards the Panchala with great speed.

verses.sanskrit: प्रादुरासीदुभयतो राजन्मध्यगतेऽहनि । पञ्चालास्तु महाराज त्वरिता विजिगीषवः ॥४२॥
verses.english: Then, O best of men, countless men, horses and elephant of both parties fell just when the sun ascended the meridian.

verses.sanskrit: ते सर्वेऽभ्यद्रवन्कर्णं पतत्रिण इव द्रुमम् । तांस्तथाधिरथिः क्रुद्धो यतमानान्मनस्विनः ॥४३॥
verses.english: The Panchalas, O king, desirous of victory, rushed towards Karna as birds flock towards their nest.

verses.sanskrit: विचिन्वन्निव बाणौघैः समासादयदग्रगान् । व्याघ्रकेतुं सुशर्माणं चित्रं चोग्रायुधं जयम् ॥४४॥
verses.english: And the energetic son of Adhiratha began to oppose the Panchalas from the front with his sharp arrows marking specially their leaders, Vyaghraketu, Susharma, Chitra, Ugrayudha, Jaya, Shukla, Rochainan and the unconquerable Singhasena.

verses.sanskrit: शुक्लं च रोचमानं च सिंहसेनं च दुर्जयम् । ते वीरा रथमार्गेण परिवव्रुर्नरोत्तमम् ॥४५॥
सृजन्तं सायकान् क्रुद्धं कर्णमाहवशोभिनम् । युध्यमानांस्तु तान्दूरान्मनुजेन्द्र प्रतापवान् ॥४६॥
verses.english: All those heroes, quickly driving their cars towards Karna-the glory of the battle field, encompassed him and began to shower their sharp shafts upon that infuriated hero, the foremost of men.

verses.sanskrit: अष्टाभिरष्टौ राधेयोऽभ्यर्दयन्निशितैः शरैः । अथापरान्महाराज सूतपुत्रः प्रतापवान् ॥४७॥
verses.english: But all those eight heroes who had proceeded to combat that brave hero, the son of Radha, were sorely afflicted by him each with eight piercing arrows.

verses.sanskrit: जघान बहुसाहस्रान् योधान्युद्धविशारदान् । जिष्णुं च जिष्णुकर्माणं देवापिं भद्रमेव च ॥४८॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O king, the powerful son of charioteer killed thousands of other heroes-all skillful in the manoeuvre of war.

verses.sanskrit: दण्डं च राजन्समरे चित्रं चित्रायुधं हरिम् । सिंहकेतुं रोचमानं शलभं च महारथम् ॥४९॥
verses.english: Worked up with anger Karna stuck in battle, Jishnu, Jishnukarman, Devapi, Bhadra, Danda, Chitra, Chitrayudha, Hari, Singhaketu, Rochamana, the great car-warriors Shalabha and many other Chedi heroes.

verses.sanskrit: निजघान सुसंक्रुद्धश्चेदीनां च महारथान् । तेषामाददतः प्राणानासीदाधिरथेर्वपुः ॥५०॥
verses.english: When the son of Adhiratha was engaged in striking those heroes his body, besmeared with blood and swelled with pride and animation, looked like the gigantic form of Rudra himself.

verses.sanskrit: शोणिताभ्युक्षिताङ्गस्य रुद्रस्येवोर्जितं महत् । तत्र भारत कर्णेन मातङ्गास्ताडिताः शरैः ॥५१॥
सर्वतोऽभ्यद्रवन् भीताः कुर्वन्तो महदाकुलम् । निपेतुरुर्व्यां समरे कर्णसायकताडिताः ॥५२॥
verses.english: Then, O Bharata, the elephants afflicted by Karna's arrows, bolted with fear and caused great commotion in the battle-field.

verses.sanskrit: कुर्वन्तो विविधान्नादान्वज्रनुन्ना इवाचलाः । गज-वाजि-मनुष्यैश्च निपतद्भिः समन्ततः ॥५३॥
verses.english: Others, oppressed by Karna's arrows, cried aloud in diverse voice and fell down as do the mountain peaks when struck down with thunder.

verses.sanskrit: रथैश्चाधिरथेर्मार्गे समास्तीर्यत मेदिनी । नैवं भीष्मो न च द्रोणो नान्ये युधि च तावकाः ॥५४॥
verses.english: The earth, along the trace of Karna's car, was fully strewn with broken cars and carcasses of elephants, horses and men.

verses.sanskrit: चक्रः स्म तादृशं कर्म यादृशं वै कृतं रणे । सूतपुत्रेण नागेषु हयेषु च रथेषु च ॥५५॥
verses.english: Verily one of the warriors of your army may not even Bhishma or Drona, did ever achieve such an exploit, as was achieved by Karna in the battle.

verses.sanskrit: नरेषु च महाराज कृतं स्म कदनं महत् । मृगमध्ये यथा सिंहो दृश्यते निर्भयश्चरन् ॥५६॥
verses.english: Suta's son, O most valiant of men, indeed made a havoc amongst the elephants and horses and destroyed the cars and men in countless numbers.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्चालानां तथा मध्ये कर्णोऽचरदभीतवत् । यथा मृगगणांस्त्रस्तान्सिंहो द्रावयते दिशः ॥५७॥
verses.english: Like a lion roaming fearlessly among a herd of deer Karna too moved about fcarlessly amongst the Panchalas.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्चालानां रथव्रातान् कर्णो व्यद्रावयत्तथा । सिहास्यं च यथा प्राप्य न जीवन्ति मृगाः क्वचित् ॥५८॥
verses.english: As a lion drives away a herd of timid deer in all directions, so Karna dispelled the crowd of Panchala's cars to all directions.

verses.sanskrit: तथा कर्णमनुप्राप्य न जिजीवुर्महारथाः । वैश्वानरं यथा प्राप्य प्रतिदह्यन्ति वै जनाः ॥५९॥
verses.english: And as a stag cam never escape from the black jaws of a lion so even those heroes, who happened to approach Karna, could not return with their lives.

verses.sanskrit: कर्णाग्निना वने तद्वद्दग्धा भारत सुञ्जयाः । कर्णेन चेदिकैकेयपाञ्चालेषु च भारत ॥६०॥
verses.english: As men are sure to be burnt down if they approach a blazing fire so even the Srinjayas, O Bharata, were burnt by the flame of Karna when they approached it.

verses.sanskrit: विश्राव्य नाम निहता बहवः शूरसंमताः । मम चासीन्मती राजन्दृष्ट्वा कर्णस्य विक्रमम् ॥६१॥
verses.english: Many proud and well-approved heroes of the Chedis and Panchalas were killed by Karna.

verses.sanskrit: नैकोऽप्याधिरथेर्जीवन्पाञ्चाल्यो मोक्ष्यते युधि । पञ्चालान्व्यधमत्संख्ये सूतपुत्रः पुनः पुनः ॥६२॥
verses.english: Beholding the valour of Karna, O king, I was under the impression that not even a single soul of the Panchalas would escape from the son of Adhiratha in that battle. Indeed the Suta's son repeatedly routed the Panchalas in the battle.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्चालानथ निघ्नन्तं कर्णं दृष्ट्वा महारणे । अभ्यधावत्सुसंक्रुद्धो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिरः ॥६३॥
verses.english: Beholding the Panchalas thus slain by Karna in that terrible battle Dharma-Raja Yudhishthira wrathfully rushed towards him.

verses.sanskrit: धृष्टद्युम्नश्च राधेयं द्रौपदेयाश्च मारिष । परिवव्रुरभित्रघ्नं शतशश्चापरे जनाः ॥६४॥
verses.english: Dhristadyumna, the sons of Droupadi and hundreds of other heroes, O Sire, speedily encompassed the son of Radha, the slayer of foes.

verses.sanskrit: शिखण्डी सहदेवश्च नकुलो नाकुलिस्तथा । जनमेजयः शिनेर्नप्ता बहवश्च प्रभद्रकाः ॥६५॥
verses.english: And many other warriors of immeasurable strength as Sikhandin, Sahadeva, Nakula, his sons, the descendant of Sini and a good many of the Prabhadrakas advancing along with Dhristadyumna in their respective cars looked very grand when they all began to strike Karna with their shafts and many other weapons of different descriptions.

verses.sanskrit: एते पुरोगमा भूत्वा धृष्टद्युम्नश्च संयुगे । कर्णमस्यन्तमिष्वस्त्रैर्विचेरुरमितौजसः ॥६६॥
तांस्तत्राधिरथिः संख्ये चेदिपाञ्चालपाण्डवान् । एको बहूनभ्यपतद्गरुत्मान्पन्नगानिव ॥६७॥
verses.english: But the son of Adhiratha, though singlehanded, fell ferociously upon all those Panchalas, Chedis and Pandavas in the encounter just as Garuda falls upon a number of snakes.

verses.sanskrit: तैः कर्णस्याभवद्युद्धं घोररूपं विशांपते । तादृग्यादृक्पुरा वृत्तं देवानां दानवैः सह ॥६८॥
verses.english: The battle, O monarch, that was fought between Karna and those warriors, became as fierce as the great battle that, in the days of yore, occurred between the gods and Asuras.

verses.sanskrit: तान् समेतान्महेष्वासान् शरवर्षौघवर्षिणः। एको व्यधमदव्यग्रस्तमांसीव दिवाकरः ॥६९॥
verses.english: Like unto the rising sun dispelling darkness the single-handed Karna unhesitatingly encountered the united force of all those great warriors ceaselessly showering sharp shafts upon him.

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनस्तु संसक्ते राधेये पाण्डवैः सह । सर्वतोऽभ्यहनत्क्रुद्धो यमदण्डनिभैः शरैः । वाहीकान्केकयान्मत्स्यान् वासात्यान्मद्रसैन्धवान् ॥७०॥
verses.english: While Karna was thus engaged with the Pandavas, Bhimasena, extremely exercised with anger, began to wound the Kurus with his shafts each of which was as sure as the very rod of Yama. That great bowman, struggling alone with all those Balhikas, Kaikeyas, Matsyas, Vasatiyas, Madras and the Saindhavas, looked exceedingly grand.

verses.sanskrit: एकः संख्ये महेष्वासो योधयन्बह्वशोभत । तत्र मर्मसु भीमेन नाराचैस्ताडिता गजाः ॥७१॥
प्रपतन्तो हतारोहाः कम्पयन्ति स्म मेदिनीम् । वाजिनश्च हतारोहाः पत्तयश्च गतासवः ॥७२॥
verses.english: The earth itself began to tremble with the violence of the fall of the huge elephants struck fatally with the awful arrows of Bhimasena in the vital parts of their riders shot dead.

verses.sanskrit: शेरते युधि निर्भिन्ना वमन्तो रुधिरं बहु । सहस्रशश्च रथिनः पातिताः पातितायुधाः ॥७३॥
verses.english: Many horses also, with their riders slain and many of the infantries lay down dead pierced with arrows and vomiting blood and bleeding profusely.

verses.sanskrit: ते क्षताः समदृश्यन्त भीमभीता गतासवः । रथिभिः सादिभिः सूतैः पादातैर्वाजिभिर्गजैः ॥७४॥
verses.english: Thousands of car-warriors, deprived of their arms, lay senseless through the fear of Bhima and inany lay dead, their bodies mangled with wounds.

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनशरैश्छिन्नैराच्छन्ना वसुधाऽभवत् । तत्स्तम्भितमिवातिष्ठद्भीमसेनभयार्दितम् ॥७५॥
verses.english: Dead bodies of elephants and their drivers, horses and riders, cars and car-warriors and foot soldiers shot dead by Bhimasena, literally covered the battle-field.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनबलं सर्वं निरुत्साहं कृतव्रणम् । निश्चेष्टं तुमुलं दीनं बभौ तस्मिन्महारणे ॥७६॥
verses.english: The army of Duryodhana, of Duryodhana, O king, melancholy, mainted and grieved through fear of Bhimasena, stood in utter confusion. That poor confounded host stood motionless in the field.

verses.sanskrit: प्रसन्नसलिले काले यथा स्यात्सागरो नृप । तद्वत्तव बलं तद्वै निश्चलं समवस्थितम् ॥७७॥
verses.english: O king, the deep ocean remains quiet in a fair season stood motionless as deep ocean remains clam and quiet in a fair weather season. Your army, in that batile, became poorly and thoroughly insert.

verses.sanskrit: मन्युवीर्यबलोपेतं दर्पात्प्रत्यवरोपितम् । अभवत्तव पुत्रस्य तत्सैन्यं निष्प्रभं तदा ॥७८॥
verses.english: The army of your son, however powerful and energetic it might have been, lost all its glory and pride at that time.

verses.sanskrit: तद्बलं भरतश्रेष्ठ वध्यमानं परस्परम् । रुधिरौघपरिक्लिन्नं रुधिरार्द्रं बभूव ह ॥७९॥
verses.english: That army, O foremost of the Bharata, when fighting with one another looked as if bathed in blood and went on killing one another.

verses.sanskrit: जगाम भरतश्रेष्ठ वध्यमानं परस्परम् । सूतपुत्रो रणे क्रुद्धः पाण्डवानामनीकिनीम् ॥८०॥
verses.english: Suta's son, filled with anger, routed the Pandava army while the enraged Bhimasena routed the Kurus. And both the heroes thus engaged looked exceedingly beautiful.

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनः कुरूंश्चापि द्रावयन्तौ विरेजतुः । वर्तमाने तथा रौद्रे संग्रामेऽद्भुतदर्शने ॥८१॥
verses.english: In that extremely fierce and awe-inspiring battle, Arjuna, that foremost of victorious heroes, having killed a large number of Samasaptakas in the very heart of their array,

verses.sanskrit: निहत्य पृतनामध्ये संशप्तकगणान्बहून् । अर्जुनो जयतां श्रेष्ठो वासुदेवमथाब्रवीत् ॥८२॥
प्रभग्नं बलमेतद्धि योत्स्यमानं जनार्दन । एते द्रवन्ति सगणाः संशप्तकमहारथाः ॥८३॥
verses.english: This array of these fighting warriors, O Janaradana, has been broken through. These great warriors of the Samasaptakas, unable to withstand my arrows, are running away with their men as a herd of deer at the roar of a lion.

verses.sanskrit: अपारयन्तो मद्बाणान्सिंहशब्दं मृगा इव । दीर्यते च महत्सैन्यं सृञ्जयानां महारणे ॥८४॥
हस्तिकक्षो ह्यसौ कृष्ण केतुः कर्णस्य धीमतः । दृश्यते राजसैन्यस्य मध्ये विचरतो मुदा ॥८५॥
verses.english: And even the vast force of the Srinjayas appears to give way in this great battle. There in the midst of Yudhishthira's division, the banner, of the highly intelligent Karna, bearing the device of an elephant is seen to move about with great activity.

verses.sanskrit: न च कर्णं रणे शक्ता जेतुमन्ये महारथाः । जानीते हि भवान् कर्णं वीर्यवन्तं पराक्रमे ॥८६॥
verses.english: O Janardana, You are well aware of Karna's energy and prowess. No other warrior of our army is capable of conquering Karna.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र याहि यतः कर्णो द्रावयत्येष नो बलम् । वर्जयित्वा रणे याहि सूतपुत्रं महारथम् ॥८७॥
verses.english: Pray, proceed there where Karna is crushing down our force. Leaving all others proceed against that mighty car-warrior, the son of Suta, O Krishna, this is my suggestion; but please do what you think proper,

verses.sanskrit: एतन्मे रोचते कृष्ण यथा वा तव रोचते । एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य गोविन्दः प्रहसन्निव ॥८८॥
अब्रवीद‌र्जुनं तूर्णं कौरवाञ्जहि पाण्डव । ततस्तव महासैन्यं गोविन्दप्रेरिता हयाः ॥८९॥
verses.english: Hearing these words of his, Govind smiled and addressing Arjuna said-"O son of Pandu, go on killing the Kauravas indiscriminately."

verses.sanskrit: हंसवर्णाः प्रविविशुर्वहन्तः कृष्णपाण्डवौ । केशवप्रेरितैरश्वैः श्वेतैः काञ्चनभूषणैः ॥९०॥
verses.english: Then those swan white horses, driven by Krishna, penetrated into your strong array bearing both Krishna and himself and the son of Pandu.

verses.sanskrit: प्रविशद्भिस्तव बलं चतुर्दिशमभिद्यत । मेघस्तनितनिर्ह्रादः स रथो वानरध्वजः ॥९१॥
verses.english: And your host gave way on all sides as those two white animals bedecked with golden trappings entered into its midst led by Keshava.

verses.sanskrit: चलत्पताकस्तां सेनां विमानं द्यामिवाविशत् । तौ विदार्य महासेनां प्रविष्टौ केशवार्जुनौ ॥९२॥
verses.english: That ape bannered car hoisting its flags in the sky and roaring like thunder-bolt cloud forced its way into your array like a celestial car passing through the welkin.

verses.sanskrit: क्रुद्धौ संरम्भरक्ताक्षौ विभ्राजेतां महाद्युती । युद्धशौण्डौ समाहूतावागतौ तौ रणाध्वरम् ॥९३॥
verses.english: When cutting through the vast army, Keshava and Arjuna entered the arena with their eyes blooded with anger they looked exceedingly splendid and resplendent.

verses.sanskrit: यज्वभिर्विधिनाहूतौ मखे देवाविवाश्विनौ । क्रुद्धौ तौ तु नरव्याघ्रौ योगवन्तौ बभूवतुः ॥९४॥
verses.english: Taking great delight in battle and accepting the challenge of the Kurus when those two heroes came to the field they looked like the w twin gods Ashvinis invoked with proper rites in a sacrifice by the priests.

verses.sanskrit: तलशब्देन रुषितौ यथा नागौ महावने । विगाह्य तु रथानीकमश्वसङ्घांश्च फाल्गुनः ॥९५॥
verses.english: Those two enraged heroes of tigerish fierceness grew extremely violent in their moments like two elephants excited at the claps of hunters in a deep forest.

verses.sanskrit: व्यचरत्पृतनामध्ये पाशहस्त इवान्तकः । तं दृष्ट्वा युधि विक्रान्तं सेनायां तव भारत ॥९६॥
verses.english: Penetrating into the midst of those cars and horses drawn in array Phalguna move about like the destroyer himself armed with his fatal noose.

verses.sanskrit: संशप्तकगणान्भूयः पुत्रस्ते समचूचुदत् । ततो रथसहस्त्रेण द्विरदानां त्रिभिः शतैः ॥९७॥
verses.english: Beholding him displaying such courage within his own army, O Bharata, your son tried once more to stir up the Samasaptakas against him.

verses.sanskrit: चतुर्दशसहस्रैस्तु तुरगाणां महाहवे । द्वाभ्यां शतसहस्राभ्यां पदातीनां च धन्विनाम् ॥९८॥
verses.english: Thereupon with thousand cars, three hundred elephants, fourteen thousand horses and two hundred thousand valiant footsoldiers, all well practised in aiming and highly skillful in all the ways of war and well armed with bows, the leaders of the Samanaptakas rushed towards the son of Kunti and covered the Pandavas, O king, with showers of shafts from all sides.

verses.sanskrit: शूराणां लब्धलक्षाणां विदितानां समन्ततः । अभ्यवर्तन्त कौन्तेयं छादयन्तो महारथाः ॥९९॥
शरवर्षैर्महाराज सर्वतः पाण्डुनन्दनम् । स च्छाद्यमानः समरे शरैः परबलार्दनः ॥१००॥
दर्शयन् रौद्रमात्मानं पाशहस्त इवान्तकः । निघ्नन्संशप्तकान्पार्थः प्रेक्षणीयतरोऽभवत् ॥१०१॥
verses.english: Covered with arrows Partha, that repressor of foes, in fight, looked exceedingly fearful like the destroyer himself with the noose in his hand, but he grew still more fierce and worth looking at when he began to kill the Samasaptakas.

verses.sanskrit: ततो विद्युत्प्रभैर्बाणैः कार्तस्वरविभूषितैः । निरन्तरमिवाकाशमासीच्छन्नं किरीटिना ॥१०२॥
verses.english: Thereupon the sky became enveloped with the arrows mounted with gold and possessed of the lustre of the lightning that were being constantly discharged by Kiriti (Arjuna).

verses.sanskrit: किरीटिभुजनिर्मुक्तैः संपतद्भिर्महाशरैः । समाच्छन्नं बभौ सर्वं काद्रवेयैरिव प्रभो ॥१०३॥
verses.english: Indeed those arrows, that were ceaselessly being discharged by Arjuna, falling on all sides looked, O lord, as if so many snakes were lying all around.

verses.sanskrit: रुक्मपुङ्खान्प्रसन्नाग्राञ्छरान्सन्नतपर्वणः । अवासृजद‌मेयात्मा दिक्षु सर्वासु पाण्डवः ॥१०४॥
verses.english: The immeasurably energetic son of Pandu sent out his straight and sharp-pointed shafts towards all directions.

verses.sanskrit: मही वियद्दिशः सर्वाः समुद्रा गिरयोऽपि वा । स्फुटन्तीति जना जज्ञुः पार्थस्य तलनिःस्वनात् ॥१०५॥
verses.english: Hearing the terrible sound of Parth's palms people thought that all the oceans, the whole earth, all the ten directions, the ethereal vault were going to burst out.

verses.sanskrit: हत्वा दशसहस्राणि पार्थिवानां महारथः । संशप्तकानां कौन्तेयः प्रत्यक्षं त्वरितोऽभ्ययात् ॥१०६॥
verses.english: Having killed ten thousand of the chiefs, that great car-warrior the son of Kunti proceeded rapidly to the further end of the Samasaptakas array.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्यक्षं च समासाद्य पार्थः काम्बोजरक्षितम् । प्रममाथ बलं बाणैर्दानवानिव वासवः ॥१०७॥
verses.english: Approaching the wing which was being defended by Kamboja he began to harass the troops by his powerful arrows as Vasava had harassed the Danavas.

verses.sanskrit: प्रचिच्छेदाशु भल्लेन द्विषतामाततायिनाम् । शस्त्रं पाणिं तथा बाहुं तथापि च शिरांस्युत ॥१०८॥
verses.english: With his broad-headed arrows he began to chop off quickly the heads, thighs and arms with weapon in the grasp of his rivals who were desirous of killing him.

verses.sanskrit: अङ्गाङ्गावयवैश्छिन्नैर्व्यायुधास्तेऽपतन् भुवि । विष्वग्वाताभिसंभग्ना बहुशाखा इव द्रुमाः ॥१०९॥
verses.english: Deprived of all the limbs and weapons they began to fall down on earth like large trees of many big boughs hurled down by a hurricane.

verses.sanskrit: हस्त्यश्वरथपत्तीनां व्रातान्निघ्नन्तमर्जुनम् । सुदक्षिणादवरजः शरवृष्ट्याऽभ्यवीवृषत् ॥११०॥
verses.english: The younger brother of Sudakshina, the king of Kamboja started shooting volley of arrows on Arjuna, the great warrior capable of killing numerous cluster of elephants, horses, chariots and infantry soldiers.

verses.sanskrit: तस्यास्यतोर्धचन्द्राभ्यां बाहू परिघसन्निभौ । पूर्णचन्द्राभवक्त्रं च क्षुरेणाभ्यहरच्छिरः ॥१११॥
verses.english: Arjuna then cut-off the two arms of his assailant with a pair of crescent-shaped arrows and then with razor-headed arrow he knocked down his head containing a face as beautiful as the full moon.

verses.sanskrit: स पपात ततो वाहात्सुलोहितपरिस्रवः । मनःशिलागिरेः शृङ्गं वज्रेणेवावदारितम् ॥११२॥
verses.english: His like extinguished, the body bathed in blood fell down from his car like the summit of Manashila mountain clapped down by a thunder-bolt.

verses.sanskrit: सुदक्षिणादवरजं काम्बोजं ददृशुर्हतम् । प्रांशुं कमलपत्राक्षमत्यर्थं प्रियदर्शनम् ॥११३॥
verses.english: When this most beautiful and handsomelooking young man, the younger brother of Sudakshina and chief of the Kambojas whose beautiful and lovely eyes could be compared with the lotus-petals, lay down dead on the ground it appeared as if the summit of the golden Sumeru was tumbled down on earth.

verses.sanskrit: काञ्चनस्तम्भसदृशं भिन्नं हेमगिरिं यथा । ततोऽभवत्पुनर्युद्धं घोरमत्यर्थमद्भुतम् ॥११४॥
नानावस्थाश्च योधानां बभूवुस्तत्र युद्ध्यताम् । एकेषुनिहतैरश्वैः काम्बोजैर्यवनैः शकैः ॥११५॥
verses.english: And the battle, that was fought after this, was exceedingly terrible and awe-inspiring and the fate of each of the fighting combatants changed repeatedly.

verses.sanskrit: शोणिताक्तैस्तदा रक्तं सर्वमासीद्विशांपते । रथैर्हताश्वसूतैश्च हतारोहैश्च वाजिभिः ॥११६॥
verses.english: All the heroes of the Kambojas, Yavanas and the Sakas were killed by one arrow each and their bleeding bodies, O king, gave the battle-field the look of a vast expanse of red.

verses.sanskrit: द्विरदैश्च हतारोहैर्महामात्रैर्हतद्विपैः । अन्योन्येन महाराज कृतो घोरो जनक्षयः ॥११७॥
तस्मिन्प्रपक्षे पक्षे च निहते सव्यसाचिना । अर्जुनं जयतां श्रेष्ठं त्वरितो द्रौणिरभ्ययात् ॥११८॥
verses.english: When the wing and further wing of the Samasaptakas had been thus eradicated by Savyasachin (Arjuna) the son of Drona rapidly proceeded against him. Furnished with many terrible arrows and violently shaking his formidable bow Drona's son appeared in the battle-field as the sun appears in the horizon with his fierce rays.

verses.sanskrit: विधुन्वानो महच्चापं कार्तस्वरविभूषितम् । आददानः शरान् घोरान् स्वरश्मीनिव भास्करः ॥११९॥
क्रोधामर्षविवृत्तास्यो लोहिताक्षो बभौ बली । अन्तकाले यथा क्रुद्धो मृत्युः किं करदण्डभृत् ॥१२०॥
verses.english: Full of rage and revengeful spirit the mighty warrior, with his mouth wide open and blood red eyes, looked formidable like Death himself with his terrible mace before a dying person.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रासृजदुग्राणि शरवर्षाणि सङ्घशः । तैर्विसृष्टैर्महाराज व्यद्रवत्पाण्डवी चमूः ॥१२१॥
verses.english: Then he began to shower sharp shafts on the armies of the Pandavas and rout them.
verses.bhavadeepa: किं करवद्दण्डं बिभर्ति किंकरनामानं वा दण्डं बिभर्ति सः ॥१२०॥

verses.sanskrit: स दृष्ट्वैव तु दाशार्हं स्यन्दनस्थं विशांपते । पुनः प्रासृजदुग्राणि शरवर्षाणि मारिष ॥१२२॥
verses.english: Again, O king, as soon as he saw the Dasarha on the car he began to discharge his terrible shafts much more quickly.

verses.sanskrit: तैः पतद्भिर्महाराज द्रौणिमुक्तैः समन्ततः । सञ्छादितौ रथस्थौ तावुभौ कृष्णधनञ्जयौ ॥१२३॥
verses.english: And their dangerous arrows discharged by Drona's son, O king, falling on Krishna and Dhananjaya, entirely enshrouded both of them on their car.

verses.sanskrit: ततः शरशतैस्तीक्ष्णैरश्वत्थामा प्रतापवान् । निश्चेष्टौ तावुभौ युद्धे कृत्वा माधवपाण्डवौ ॥१२४॥
verses.english: And thus the violent Ashvatthama, with hundreds of keen arrows, put both Madhava and Pandu's son into utter confusion.

verses.sanskrit: हाहाकृतमभूत्सर्वं स्थावरं जङ्गमं तथा । चराचरस्य गोप्तारौ दृष्ट्वा संछादितौ शरैः ॥१२५॥
verses.english: Beholding those two guardians of the world, thus covered with arrows, the creation sent forth piteous cries of woe.

verses.sanskrit: सिद्धचारणसंघाश्च संपेतुस्ते समन्ततः । चिन्तयन्तो भवेदद्य लोकानां स्वस्त्यपीति च ॥१२६॥
verses.english: There hordes of Siddhas and Charanas poured in form every direction all solicitous of common weal for the day.

verses.sanskrit: न मया तादृशो राजन् दृष्टपूर्वः पराक्रमः । संग्रामे यादृशो द्रौणेः कृष्णौ संछाद‌यिष्यतः ॥१२७॥
verses.english: Never before, O monarch, did I witness such prodigies of valor like those displayed by Drouni when shrouding Krishna and Arjuna in the field.

verses.sanskrit: द्रौणेस्तु धनुषः शब्द‌महितत्रासनं रणे । अश्रौषं बहुशो राजन् सिंहस्य निनदो यथा ॥१२८॥
verses.english: Often and often did I hear in that battle, O king, the din of Drouni's volleys, thundering roars of lion to the consternation of the enemy.

verses.sanskrit: ज्या चास्य चरतो युद्धे सव्यद‌क्षिणमस्यतः । विद्युदम्बुदमध्यस्था भ्राजमानेव साऽभवत् ॥१२९॥
verses.english: Flinging his shots right and left as he moved round the field, the string of his bow shone like flashes of lightning sparkling amidst the cloudy heavens.

verses.sanskrit: स तथा क्षिप्रकारी च दृढहस्तश्च पाण्डवः । प्रमोहं परमं गत्वा प्रेक्षन्तं द्रोणजं ततः ॥१३०॥
verses.english: Inspite of the dexterity and inflexibility of his hand, the son of Pandu, beholding the son of Drona, at the time, was greatly bewildered. And he (Arjuna) bethought himself of being deprived of his own prowess by that august personage (Ashvatthaman), whose bearing in the field, O king, presented a dazzling sight for human eyes.

verses.sanskrit: विक्रमं विहतं मेने आत्मनः स महायशाः । तस्यास्य समरे राजन्वपुरासीत्सुदुर्दृशम् ॥१३१॥
द्रौणिपाण्डवयोरेवं वर्तमाने महारणे । वर्धमाने च राजेन्द्र द्रोणपुत्रे महाबले ॥१३२॥
verses.english: In that deadly conflict between Drouni and the Pandava, O king of kings Krishna, seeing the powerful son of Drona get the better of the son of Kunti, became highly infuriated.

verses.sanskrit: हीयमाने च कौन्तेये कृष्णे रोषः समाविशत् । स रोषान्निःश्वसन् राजन्निर्दहन्निव चक्षुषा ॥१३३॥
द्रौणिं ह्यपश्यत्संग्रामे फाल्गुनं च मुहुर्मुहुः । ततः क्रुद्धोऽब्रवीत्कृष्णः पार्थं सप्रणयं तदा ॥१३४॥
verses.english: With inflamed eyes and swelling breath, frequently he cast his eyes towards. Ashvatthama and Phalguna, devouring them, as it were, with the fury of his fire.

verses.sanskrit: अत्यद्भुतमिदं पार्थ तव पश्यामि संयुगे । अतिशेते हि यत्र त्वां द्रोणपुत्रोऽद्य भारत ॥१३५॥
verses.english: The indignant Krishna then addressing Partha in an endearing tone and said-O Partha, what a strange part of, see, you play in the field? O son of Bharata, Drona's son overcoming you today in battle!

verses.sanskrit: कच्चिद्वीर्यं यथापूर्वं भूजयोर्वा बलं तव । कच्चित्ते गाण्डिवं हस्ते रथे तिष्ठसि चार्जुन ॥१३६॥
verses.english: Have you the same strength of your arms as you had before? Do you still hold your Gandiva in hand? Are you seated in the warchariot?

verses.sanskrit: कच्चित्कुशलिनो बाहू मुष्टिर्वा न व्यशीर्यत । उदीर्यमाणं हि रणे पश्यामि द्रौणिमाहवे ॥१३७॥
verses.english: Has nay thing gone wrong with your arms? Has your fist sustained any injury, or how is it that I see you overwhelmed by Drouni in the field.

verses.sanskrit: गुरुपुत्र इति ह्येनं मानयन् भरतर्षभ । उपेक्षां कुरु मा पार्थ नायं काल उपेक्षितुम् ॥१३८॥
verses.english: O glory of Bharata's race, esteeming your assailant as the son of your preceptor stop not, O Partha, this is not the time for forbearance.

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्तु कृष्णेन गृह्य भल्लांश्चतुर्दश । त्वरमाणस्त्वराकाले द्रौणेर्धनुरथाच्छिनत् ॥१३९॥
verses.english: Hearing those words Arjuna just on the nick of time seizing fourteen Bhallas (arrows, with crescent-shaped heads) darted them off, piercing right through his weapons, chariot, standard and umbrella and dismantling Ashvatthama of his equipment's, bows, darts and all. He (Arjuna), then assailing him (Ashvatthama) with calf-toothed arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ध्वजं छत्रं पताकाश्च रथं शक्तिं गदां तथा । जत्रुदेशे च सुभृशं वत्सदन्तैरताडयत् ॥१४०॥
स मूर्छां परमां गत्वा ध्वजयष्टिं समाश्रितः । तं विसंज्ञं महाराज शत्रुणा भृशपीडितम् ॥१४१॥
verses.english: Inflicted terrible wounds on his shoulderjoints fainting from which he sustained himself with his flag-staff. Seeing him thus stunned with the assaults of his enemy his charioteer, O monarch, for rescuing him from (the army of) Dhananjaya bore him away from the field.

verses.sanskrit: अपोवाह रणात्सूतो रक्षमाणो धनञ्जयः । एतस्मिन्नेव काले च विजयः शत्रुतापनः ॥१४२॥
verses.english: O Bharata, In the meanwhile, that scorcher of enemy, Vijay, before the very eyes of your valiant son slaughtered your army by hundreds and thousands.

verses.sanskrit: व्यहनत्तावकं सैन्यं शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः । पश्यतस्तस्य वीरस्य तव पुत्रस्य भारत ॥१४३॥
एवमेष क्षयो वृत्तस्तावकानां परैः सह । क्रूरो विशसनो घोरो राजन् दुर्मन्त्रिते तव ॥१४४॥
verses.english: Thus, O monarch, owing to your evil counsels such a ruthless slaughter with cruel onslaught of your champions was brought about as these knights presented arms to your foe.

verses.sanskrit: संशप्तकांश्च कौन्तेयः कुरूंश्चापि वृकोदरः । वसुषेणश्च पञ्चालान् क्षणेन व्यधमद्रणे ॥१४५॥
verses.english: Arjuna then in the twinkle of an eye beset the Samasaptakas, while Vrikodara attacked the Kurus and Karna attacked the Panchalas.

verses.sanskrit: वर्तमाने तथा रौद्रे राजन्वीरवरक्षये । उत्थितान्यगणेयानि कबन्धानि समन्ततः ॥१४६॥
verses.english: O monarch, as the war raged furiously, destroying the lives of valiant soldiers and presenting a vast scene of carnage, there arose in the field innumerable headless trunks, still retaining vitality.

verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिरोऽपि संग्रामे प्रहारैर्गाढवेदनः । क्रोशमात्रमपक्रम्य तस्थौ भरतसत्तमः ॥१४७॥
verses.english: O the chief of the Bharata race, king Yudhishthira, sorely distressed with his wounds and writhing in agony, stayed in the time two miles off from the scene of action.
